subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm 58 years old and female. I'm here because I've been having left shoulder pain for a few weeks now. It's been really bothering me, especially when I try to move my arm or sleep on my side. Doctor: Could you please provide your age, gender, and describe the nature of your left shoulder pain, including when it started, its intensity, and any associated symptoms? Patient: I'm 58 and female. The pain started a few weeks ago, and it's been constant. It really hurts when I try to move my arm or lift anything, and I can't even raise it over my head. It's especially bad when I try to sleep on my left side, and it's always there, even when I'm not doing anything. I've been taking Tylenol, and that helps a little, but the pain is still pretty bad most of the time. Doctor: Could you describe the nature of the shoulder pain (e.g., sharp, dull, burning) and whether it radiates to other areas? Have you noticed any swelling, redness, numbness, or tingling in the shoulder or arm? Have you had any recent trauma or injury to the shoulder, and have you undergone any prior treatments or interventions for this issue? Patient: The pain is more of a dull, aching sensation, and it doesn't really radiate anywhere else. I don't have any swelling, redness, numbness, or tingling. I haven't had any recent trauma or injury to the shoulder, and I haven't had any prior treatments for this specific issue before today. Doctor: Have you experienced any stiffness in the shoulder, particularly in the morning or after periods of inactivity? If so, how long does it last? Patient: I don't really have stiffness in the morning or after being inactive, but the pain is always there no matter what I do. It doesn't get better with rest or anything like that. Doctor: Could you please describe any physical examination findings related to your shoulder
